confirmed_problem_statement: Select an algorithmic strategy (e.g., CNN/U‑Net, transformer, physics‑informed unmixing, or hybrid) to recover the 10 m sub‑pixel layout from a 30 m pixel and design mechanisms (custom loss, constraint layers, post‑processing projection, consistency regularization) that guarantee the 3 × 3 sub‑pixel predictions, when averaged, exactly reproduce the original 30 m pixel’s class composition.
search_queries_used: recover 10m sub-pixel layout from 30m satellite pixel using deep learning
CNN U-Net transformer hybrid spectral unmixing upsampling for sub-pixel classification
subpixel classification tool with constraint layers and custom loss for composition consistency
open source implementation of physics-informed unmixing network for sub-pixel resolution
closest_match_summary: Several recent works combine spectral unmixing with deep‑learning‑based super‑resolution (CNN/U‑Net, transformer hybrids) and introduce constraint‑oriented losses to preserve class proportions. The most directly relevant are hybrid frameworks that explicitly enforce composition consistency via hard constraints or projection layers, though none demonstrate a strict equality guarantee for a 3 × 3 upsampling from 30 m to 10 m.

candidates.name: A Hybrid Framework for Sub-Pixel Target Detection Using Spectral Unmixing, Super-Resolution, and Deep Learning in Satellite Imagery
candidates.notes: Combines spectral unmixing, CNN‑based super‑resolution, and a custom loss that penalizes deviation from the original pixel composition. Does not enforce exact equality but is the closest published hybrid approach.

candidates.name: Hard-Constrained Hopfield Neural Network for Subpixel Mapping
candidates.notes: Introduces a Hopfield network with hard constraints that force the sum of sub‑pixel class probabilities to match the coarse‑pixel label exactly. Focuses on binary/ternary classes; extension to 3 × 3 multi‑class layout would require adaptation.

candidates.name: Dual-Branch Subpixel-Guided Network for Hyperspectral Image Classification
candidates.notes: Two‑branch architecture: one branch learns spectral unmixing, the other learns spatial upsampling. Uses a composition‑preserving loss but only approximates the average constraint.

candidates.name: Explicable Sub-Pixel Mapping Based on Nested Self-Attention Network with Spatial Correlation Learnable Mechanism
candidates.notes: Self‑attention network that explicitly models spatial correlation for sub‑pixel mapping; includes a regularizer encouraging the summed sub‑pixel probabilities to equal the coarse pixel distribution.

candidates.name: HyFormer: Hybrid Transformer and CNN for Pixel-Level Multispectral Classification
candidates.notes: Hybrid CNN‑Transformer for pixel‑wise classification; does not address sub‑pixel upsampling or composition constraints.

candidates.name: Cross-range self-attention single hyperspectral image super‑resolution (uHNTC)
candidates.notes: Hybrid Transformer‑CNN for hyperspectral super‑resolution; includes a reconstruction loss but no explicit class‑composition enforcement.

candidates.name: Deformable Transformer and Spectral U‑Net for Large‑Scale Remote Sensing Semantic Segmentation
candidates.notes: Focuses on semantic segmentation with transformer‑U‑Net; does not target sub‑pixel layout or composition constraints.

candidates.name: Integration of coarser images in subpixel mapping
candidates.notes: Conceptual discussion of using coarse imagery to inform sub‑pixel mapping; no concrete algorithm or loss formulation.

candidates.name: Techniques for deep learning with satellite & aerial imagery
candidates.notes: Curated list of resources; does not contain an implementation directly addressing the 30 m→10 m composition‑exact problem.

gaps_identified: Existing works either approximate the composition constraint with soft losses or focus on binary/ternary classes. None provide a proven mechanism that guarantees the exact equality of the averaged 3 × 3 sub‑pixel class probabilities to the original 30 m pixel distribution for multi‑class land‑cover at 10 m resolution. A novel component—such as a differentiable projection layer or a Lagrangian multiplier‑based hard constraint integrated into a CNN/U‑Net or transformer backbone—remains unaddressed, as does a benchmark on the specific 30 m→10 m (3× upsampling) scenario with quantitative verification of zero composition error.
